svg.title: Fort Henry, Kingston: the limestone casemate range on the fort's parade, square on, as photographed in 2010 and 1908-12. A long two-storey wall of pale grey limestone pierced by four tall round-headed arches on square piers, a ring of voussoirs round each arch, and inside each arch the casemate front: a door and white-framed sash windows on the ground floor, and on the upper floor a gallery behind a black iron railing with its own door and windows. Over the arches a plain spandrel wall, a projecting cornice, and the rampart parapet carrying a continuous black iron railing, a row of limestone chimney stacks, and two dark iron guns on the rampart, as the 2010 photograph shows. NO FIGURE of any kind (no re-enactor, guard, soldier or visitor), no flag or flagstaff (OQ-ART-04), no plaque, sign, lettering, crest or coat of arms. Drawn from assets/refs/kingston/fort-henry-casemates-2010.jpg, checked against fort-henry-parade-and-casemates-1908.jpg; stone tone from fort-henry-ditch-and-branch-tower-2021.jpg. Every colour is from palette.json. See assets/refs/references.json, subject fort-henry. POI hero, present at every visual tier.
